sections.name: Mushroom
sections.card:
Summary: An item that has you throw two Dice Blocks in place of one and move the combined total. An Item Shop sells it for 10 coins, and it is Mario's favorite item. Every character has a favorite, and computer players pick theirs up whenever they get the chance.
Uses: Use it on your turn to throw two Dice Blocks and walk as many spaces as the two numbers add up to. A matching pair earns 10 coins, and a pair of 7s earns 20.
Tips: At 10 coins it ties with the Skeleton Key as the cheapest item in the shop. You can hold just a single item, and while holding one you cannot walk into an Item Shop or start an Item Mini-Game, so use it before your next shop or Item Space.

sections.name: Golden Mushroom
sections.card:
Summary: An item that lets you roll three Dice Blocks and move the total of all three. It costs 20 coins at an Item Shop.
Uses: Use it to roll three Dice Blocks and move the sum of the three numbers. If all three show the same number you get 20 coins, and three 7s give you 50 coins.
Tips: It is on the shop's stock lists in the first five turns for some placings, and on every placing's list from the middle of the game on. On Bowser Land, walking past the Baby Bowser shop in a Bowser Suit makes him hand you one of four items for free: a Magic Lamp, Boo Bell, Golden Mushroom or Skeleton Key.

sections.name: Skeleton Key
sections.card:
Summary: An item that opens a locked gate on a board when you reach it, usually giving access to areas you could not otherwise reach. It costs 10 coins at an Item Shop and is Luigi's favorite item.
Uses: At a locked gate the key swings it open for you and the gate shuts again behind you. The key only opens the door, so you may spend it on a door and then not go that way.
Tips: You cannot discard it to free up a slot for something else: it stays with you until you use it on a door, unless a rival steals it. Item Shops always sell it for 10 coins, except on Bowser Land, where Baby Bowser may push one onto you for 12.

sections.name: Plunder Chest
sections.card:
Summary: An item that steals an item from an opponent. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Peach's favorite item.
Uses: Using it takes an item off one rival, picked by chance from every opponent who is holding something; you have no say in whom. The loot can be used straight away, apart from a Bowser Bomb, or kept for a later turn.
Tips: In the Item Shop it shows up for the player in second place in the middle of the game and for the player in first place in the last five turns.

sections.name: Dueling Glove
sections.card:
Summary: An item that lets you pick an opponent to duel in a Duel Mini-Game for coins. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Wario's favorite item.
Uses: Using it summons a Goomba, then you choose the opponent to duel and how many coins to wager. The most you can wager is the coin count of whichever of the two players has fewer coins before the duel.
Tips: The wager is always coins. In the Item Shop it appears in the middle of the game for third and fourth place and in the last five turns for first and second place.

sections.name: Warp Block
sections.card:
Summary: An item that swaps your place on the board with a random opponent. It costs 15 coins at an Item Shop and is Yoshi's favorite item.
Uses: The Warp Block shows up over your head when you use it. You hit it, which sends you to a random opponent's space and moves them to yours. You can still throw the ordinary Dice Block that same turn.
Tips: You can also win one from an Item Mini-Game. In the Item Shop it only shows up in the last five turns, for the players in second, third and fourth place, and on Bowser Land the forced sale costs 17 coins.

sections.name: Magic Lamp
sections.card:
Summary: An item that takes you straight to the Star Space. At 30 coins it is the most expensive item in the Item Shop.
Uses: Using it calls the Mushroom Genie, who carries you off to the Star Space. There you are asked if you would like to buy a Star for 20 coins.
Tips: You still pay 20 coins for the Star when you arrive, on top of the 30 it costs to buy. The shop offers it only in the last five turns, to third and fourth place. When Bowser's Multiplying Toads puts two Toads on the board, a Magic Lamp always takes you to the real one.

sections.name: Boo Bell
sections.card:
Summary: An item that rings for a Boo to take coins or a Star off an opponent. In this game you win it in Item Mini-Games, and neither kind of Item Shop sells it.
Uses: Using it summons a Boo, who asks whom to steal from. Stealing coins costs you five coins and stealing a Star costs 50 coins, and the Boo can take at most 30 coins or one Star.
Tips: If a Boo is stealing coins from you, press the A button quickly to fight it off. Baby Bowser's shop on Bowser Land can also give you a Boo Bell for free, as one of four possible gifts, if you pass it in a Bowser Suit.

sections.name: Bowser Suit
sections.card:
Summary: A rare item that disguises you as Bowser and lets you take 20 coins off every opponent you walk past. You usually win it in an Item Mini-Game.
Uses: Using it dresses you from head to toe as Bowser, and each opponent you pass loses 20 coins to you.
Tips: Baby Bowsers treat you differently when you wear it. The one on the board always hands you coins as you pass. On Bowser Land you may redirect the parade at no cost, except on the final move, you get 20 coins when you pass the Bowser Bank, and the forced shop gives you an item free. The normal Item Shops never sell the suit, though Baby Bowser's shop on Bowser Land can push one onto you for 12 coins.

sections.name: Bowser Bomb
sections.card:
Summary: An item you can win in an Item Mini-Game: Bowser sets it off when that turn ends, and every player he passes loses all their coins. Donkey Kong counts it as his favorite.
Uses: When the turn ends Baby Bowser changes into Bowser, hits three Dice Blocks, and travels the board by that total, snatching every coin from each player he goes by.
Tips: Apart from Item Mini-Games, the only source is the forced sale by Baby Bowser on Bowser Land, which costs 12 coins. A Bomb taken with a Plunder Chest cannot be used right away. If it goes off while two Toads stand on the board after Bowser's Multiplying Toads, it reveals which Toad is fake.

sections.name: Baby Bowser on the boards
sections.card:
Summary: A minion of Bowser who appears once on each board, next to Toad. He takes 5 coins from any player who goes by, though once in a while he hands over 5 coins and then claims it was a mistake.
Weak points: Wear a Bowser Suit and he always gives you coins instead of taking them. He begins at one of a few fixed places next to Toad, and each time the Star is bought he goes to the spot Toad just left.
Looks like: A small copy of Bowser.
Tips: Count on losing 5 coins whenever you pass him, because the gift is rare. When the turn ends, a Bowser Bomb puts Bowser in his place for a short while, and so does the Bowser's Appearing Act result on a Bowser Space roulette.

sections.name: Bowser Parade
sections.card:
Summary: A parade led by Baby Bowser that travels a set path across Bowser Land and sends anyone it catches back to the start.
Weak points: Baby Bowser calls the parade off if nobody is standing in its way when it begins. There are parade offices at the board's north, west and east crossings, where a player can pay five coins to Baby Bowser to turn the parade another way; in a Bowser Suit it costs nothing, except on the last move.
Looks like: Baby Bowser leads several pyramid-shaped floats made to look like enemies, for example a Goomba, a Boo and a Thwomp.
Tips: The parade begins every time at the middle crossing along the board's northern edge. Its first stretch goes directly south to the far end, then turns east toward where the players start.

sections.name: Big Boo
sections.card:
Summary: A giant Boo on Horror Land who, like a normal Boo, steals coins or Stars, but from every opponent at once.
Weak points: You can only ask for him at night.
Looks like: By day he is a huge Boo statue.
Tips: Because the night-time path to him needs a Skeleton Key, meeting him is difficult and rare.

sections.name: Bowser Space
sections.card:
Summary: A space that calls Bowser up; the Bowser Roulette then picks an event. It is usually bad news, or something that changes the game, for whoever landed, and it can hit the other players as well.
Weak points: If you have no coins when you land on a Coins for Bowser result, Bowser gives you 10 coins instead. The 10,000 Coin Present, 100 Star Present, Star Steal and Stars-Packed to Go results can come up on the roulette, but if one does, Bowser simply leaves and nothing happens.
Tips: Coins for Bowser is the commonest result and sits on the wheel twice. Bowser's Coin Potluck draws coins from each of the four players: 10 coins during the first five turns, 30 in the last five and 20 otherwise. Bowser's Multiplying Toads uses a "magic" trick to put two Toads on the board, which moves the Star Space and adds a second one. Pay the false Toad 20 coins and he drops the act and hands you a Ztar, which leaves your Star total unchanged. Ride a Magic Lamp and you always reach the real Toad; a Bowser Bomb exposes the fake.
